Official collision description

Both parties were travelling on Al Mursalat Street, heading north, in the middle lane. Failure by Party 1 to keep adequate distance led to a collision and property damage to both cars. The reported impacts were to the Camry’s front and Elantra’s rear. The narrative cites traffic regulation article 50/2/19.

Official report particulars

Final liability determination report; version 1, dated 13 October 2026. Case RD1310261711. Inspector/surveyor ID 5169. Location: Al Mursalat, Riyadh. Coordinates 24.737022, 46.68538. Incident parties: 2; recorded injuries: 0; recorded deaths: 0.

Important interpretation detail: The tabular “Cause of accident” text (“Not maintaining a safe distance”) is visibly duplicated beneath both party columns. However, the narrative expressly identifies Party 1 as the driver who failed to leave sufficient distance, and the determination lists 100% to Party 1 / 0% to Party 2. Do not treat the duplicated generic cause field as a 50/50 liability ruling.

05 · Evidence integrity / limitations

Cross-checks, uncertainties, and what is not proven

Case-number consistency

Case ID RD1310261711 appears in the Najm final PDF, the Najm SMS screenshot and the Taqdeer booking SMS. The repeated identifier ties those sources to the same reported incident, subject to source authenticity.

Vehicles cross-confirmed

The report’s black Camry front and white Elantra rear impact pattern is consistent with all three photographs. The images cannot establish speed, pre-impact road positioning or mechanical causation independently.

All JPEG EXIF capture metadata absent

All five uploaded JPEGs contain no readable EXIF capture-time, timezone or GPS fields. Their image pixels contain visible SMS device clocks and scene details, but there is no independent camera-timestamp proof in the uploaded versions.

SMS group timestamps are not per-message receipt times

“4:02 PM” and “5:26 PM” head message groups containing multiple bubbles. Individual bubble arrival times and SMS calendar dates are not all displayed. “6:47 PM” precedes the separate Arabic Taqdeer notice.

Assessment booking vs completion

A Taqdeer appointment was booked for 7:30–8:00 PM AST on 13 October. The Arabic notice confirms assessment registration, not a completed valuation, settled claim, approved repair or payment. A “within 48 hours” statement is a service estimate, not a demonstrated outcome.

Images show damage, not medical assessment

The final Najm form records 0 reported injuries and 0 deaths. This does not rule out symptoms that emerge later, and still images cannot assess occupants’ medical condition. There are no medical records in this evidence packet.

No objective accident-time proof

The report specifically labels 3:55:14 PM as case registration time. The provided sources do not display a trustworthy exact impact time; photos carry no EXIF capture time. Any purported minute of impact would be invented.

Evidence-handling note

SHA-256 hashes identify the exact uploaded file bytes analyzed here. They do not authenticate who created each source. Screenshots and PDF files are embedded byte-for-byte; this report is a review and is not an official police/insurance certification.

Timezone policy: Everything in this HTML is expressed in Saudi time (AST, UTC+03:00), including the converted internal PDF timestamp and uploaded-file copy times. Raw original bytes remain preserved inside the embedded source files for auditing. Hijri calendar dates are retained exactly as printed; they are not timezones. Where the screenshot shows a clock without an original date, that limitation is made explicit.
